actions: Audited public GitHub ruleset layering, bypass, organization-level targeting, repository deletion/restoration, and permission requirements.

Executed a 96-scenario threat-depth model comparing ordinary CAS, one-time repository/organization guards, read-each verification, hypothetical atomic guard-epoch+ref update, external monotonic floor, and fail-closed behavior.
Separated target-ref-only rollback from guard mutation/bypass, repository reincarnation, organization-guard mutation, and platform rollback.
Persisted executable model, JSON result and checkpoint in the role-local namespace and read back the checkpoint.
Observed main-head movement after the first leaf, then verified the frozen root/config blobs remained unchanged before continuing semantic work under the same frozen tuple.

tested_scope.repo_guard_read_each_toctou: unsafe stale accept 2/2 when guard mutates after read before write
tested_scope.org_guard_read_each_toctou: unsafe stale accept 2/2 when guard mutates after read before write

generic_residual_capability_boundary.minimum_generic_effect: Place the anti-rollback trust root outside the deepest authority domain allowed to be rolled back/mutated/bypassed/deleted/restored. A one-time server guard is sufficient only if its mutation/bypass is outside the threat; read-each client verification does not close after-read/before-write mutation.
generic_residual_capability_boundary.evidence_of_unavailability: Ruleset/protection mutation is not exposed in the connected capability surface, and CLEAN policy forbids protected-authority mutation.

termination.reason: Protected-boundary depth leaf completed; recurring role remains enabled and continues to the next non-conflicting multi-agent claim leaf.

exact_continuation: Continue under the same frozen control tuple unless a newer control/config is detected. Next leaf: guard-epoch inclusion in multi-agent claims and publication certificates. Model two workers acquiring the same logical task/effect reservation under guard epoch e1, one staging under e1, then authority moving to e2 and another worker taking over. Compare claim keys omitting guard epoch, claim keys including guard epoch, sink-time server enforcement, client read-each guard verification, and a fail-closed staged integrator. Include stale result reuse, ambiguous e1 publication response, dedupe expiry, old-path replay after e2, and guard verification outage. Primary falsification: determine whether guard_epoch in claim identity actually fences stale authority or merely labels stale work unless the authoritative sink atomically checks current guard epoch.
